acceptance_conditions: V200-01 foundation and source identity are recorded.
V200-Q01 records the bounded B01 outcome and any stop condition.
V200-02 through V200-05 are completed by nonoverlapping owners.
V200-06 records actual llama consumer behavior and the tested transparency tier.
boundaries: Keep the facade application-scoped and reversible.
Do not silently narrow the supported one-logical-device-per-physical-pair contract.
Use the package probe and existing CUDA controller; do not add a scheduler or test framework.
invariants: Memory ownership, completion ordering, and observed consumer calls must not return false success.
CPU checks and compilation are not GPU qualification.
Release the GPU allocation after the bounded B01 decision; the implementation lanes do CPU work only.
charter.objective: Deliver the earliest correct, opt-in single-logical-device preview for the existing llama.cpp/llama-server workload, with pair feasibility measured early and honest evidence boundaries.

tasks.notes: Run only the existing bounded B01 probe through the approved CUDA controller. Store the pair profile and controller receipt under evidence/foundation. Use exact pair and stack identity; record case-level result. Build on the V200-01 CPU foundation. Stop at the first foundational failure, release GPU allocation, and report the negative result. Do not create a new test framework or claim full consumer qualification.
tasks.objective: Run the package existing B01 pair-memory probe on the approved V100 pair as soon as V200-01 is complete; record actual feasibility before consumer implementation concludes.
tasks.title: Qualify pair memory early with the existing bounded probe
